newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman opposes cutting EEP to $10 Mln.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman opposes cutting EEP to $10 Mln.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Monday his department was trying to dissuade Congress from limiting the major U.S. export subsidy program to $10 million, down from $100 million.

"We would not like to see that," Glickman told the National Association of Agricultural Journalists meeting. "What would justify cutting EEP (Export Enhancement Program) to almost nothing this year...?"
The cut was approved last week by a House Appropriations subcommittee as part of a disaster relief bill. The full committee will consider the bill this week.
"I don't think it's good public policy," Glickman said of the proposed cut.
USDA has not subsidized a grain sale since July 1995 but has engaged in several rounds of saber-rattling with the European Union to ensure EU retraint in its use of ag export subsidies.
The Clinton administration has asked for $500 million for EEP in fiscal 1998 -- the full amount allowed by trade rules.

Some officials said the proposed cut in fiscal 1997 EEP funding would have little practical effect because USDA was unlikely to need EEP before fall, if then. However, Glickman has said it is an important weapon in USDA's arsenal.
